title: AXI Response Ordering: Three Writes, Two IDs
description: Compare legal and illegal response sequences after Write A and Write B reuse ID 5 while Write C uses independent ID 2.

phases.name: A · ID 5
phases.description: Write A is the older transaction in ID-5's ordering stream.

phases.name: B · ID 5
phases.description: Write B reuses ID 5. Its response must not be accepted before A's response.

phases.name: C · ID 2
phases.description: Write C uses ID 2, so the AXI ID response-order rule does not order C relative to A or B.

phases.name: C · ID 2
phases.description: C can complete first because ID 2 is independent from the ID-5 response stream.

phases.name: A · ID 5
phases.description: A is the first accepted ID-5 response.

phases.name: B · ID 5
phases.description: B follows A, preserving issue order within ID 5.

phases.name: A · ID 5
phases.description: A retires first from the ID-5 queue.

phases.name: C · ID 2
phases.description: C can be placed anywhere relative to A and B as long as other system ordering constraints do not apply.

phases.name: B · ID 5
phases.description: B remains after A in the same-ID response order.

phases.name: B · ID 5 ✕
phases.description: Protocol violation: B is the younger ID-5 write but its response appears before A's response.

phases.name: C · ID 2
phases.description: C's placement is not the problem; it belongs to a different ID stream.

phases.name: A · ID 5
phases.description: A arrives too late to repair the earlier same-ID ordering violation.

annotations.message: A per-ID FIFO records A before B even though both entries use the same numeric ID.
Different IDs permit response reordering; they do not override address, memory-type, barrier, or product-specific ordering constraints elsewhere in the system.
The monitor flags the first accepted B response for ID 5 because the head of that ID's outstanding queue is still A.
